title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. K is a base field, assumed of characteristic 0 for now. L/K is a finitely generated extension of transcendence degree n, and L̄ is an algebraic closure of L. Write E_L = Gal(L̄/L) for the arithmetic Galois group. Write Π^{L̄}_{L/K} for the 'geometric' part: the kernel of E_L → E_K, i.e. Gal(L̄/LK̄). One chooses a regular model U of L/K and a codimension-1 point x of U, i.e. the generic point of a prime divisor. V = O_{U,x} is a DVR with fraction field L, residue field k(x) and S_x = Spec V.

On this page:
- Take a point x' above x in the normalisation of S_x in L̄. This gives a decomposition group N_{x'} and an inertia group I_{x'} in E_L.
- (26) N_{x'}/I_{x'} is identified with the absolute Galois group of the residue field k(x). The residue field k(x') of x' is an algebraic closure of k(x) in characteristic 0. k(x) is finitely generated over K of transcendence degree n−1.
- (27) Via Kummer theory, I_{x'} ≅ T(K̄) = lim μ_m(K̄) = Ẑ(1). In residue characteristic 0 all inertia is tame and procyclic. The left marginal note flags that in positive characteristic one would only get the ℓ-adic / prime-to-p part.
- These constructions are independent of the model (U, X) chosen; only the valuation (the divisor) matters.
- (28) I_{x'} ⊂ Π^{L̄}_{L/K}. Inertia acts trivially on the residue field, which contains K̄, so it lies in the geometric part.
- (29) Pass to the (non-strict) henselisation Ṽ of V. Set S̃_x = Spec Ṽ and Ũ_x = S̃_x minus {x} = Spec L̃_x, with L̃_x = Frac Ṽ. Grothendieck notes there is an 'exterior' homomorphism E_{Ũ_x} → E_L, defined up to conjugation. Its effective choice depends on a geometric point / universal cover of Ũ_x. The next page shows this amounts to an L-embedding L̃_x → L̄, i.e. to the choice of x'.
- Continuing (next page): N_{x'} ≅ E_{L̃_x} (local Galois group of the henselian field), and I_{x'} = ker(E_{L̃_x} → E_{k(x)}).
- He then conjectures N_{x'} = Norm_{E_L}(I_{x'}).

Purpose: this is the 'local' groundwork of the Longue Marche anabelian programme. Divisorial valuations of a function field are to be read off group-theoretically from the Galois group as inertia/decomposition subgroups, with inertia ≅ Ẑ(1) carrying the cyclotomic structure. Such data is what a birational anabelian reconstruction needs.
errors: (26) as transcribed identifies a group with a field ('≃ k(x')'). It must be read as a Galois group: N/I ≅ Gal(k(x')/k(x)) = E_{k(x)}, with k(x') = algebraic closure of k(x) in characteristic 0. The parenthetical describes k(x), not the quotient.
(27) holds only for residue characteristic 0. In characteristic p wild inertia appears and only the prime-to-p tame quotient is ≅ Π_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ(1). Grothendieck flags this himself in the margin.

Not on this page but on the next: the tentative claim I_{x'} = Norm_{Π_{L/K}}(I_{x'}) would be false as stated. N_{x'} ∩ Π_{L/K} normalizes I_{x'} and is strictly larger when n ≥ 2, since it maps onto Gal(k(x)bar/k(x)K̄), which is nontrivial. Grothendieck marks it with a question mark.

ideas.what: Decomposition and inertia groups at a prime divisor of a function field, with the quotient being the Galois group of the residue field
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. X / XIII context (tame ramification along divisors, with Murre)

ideas.what: Inertia ≅ Ẑ(1) = T(K̄) via Kummer theory in residue characteristic 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Grothendieck–Murre for the scheme version

ideas.what: Inertia lies in the geometric fundamental group Π_{L/K}, and the construction is independent of the model
ideas.modern_name: Inertia of divisorial valuations in the geometric Galois group

ideas.what: Henselisation of the DVR, giving a conjugacy class of exterior homomorphisms E_{L̃_x} → E_L whose choice corresponds to x' above x
ideas.modern_name: Local Galois group of the henselisation equals the decomposition group

ideas.what: Group-theoretic recovery of divisors from the Galois group of a function field (the motivation; the normalizer conjecture is on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Local theory of birational anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse discuss birational anabelian ideas in general terms

deep.surprise_reason: The page is standard valuation-theoretic and Galois-theoretic groundwork: decomposition and inertia at a divisor, Kummer, henselisation. It is interesting only as evidence that the Longue Marche notes set up a birational, divisor-by-divisor local theory, which was later developed independently by Pop and others. Nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: (26) the right-hand side is meant as the Galois group of k(x')/k(x) (or E_{k(x)}), not the field k(x') itself.
(27) 'T_0(L̄)' is likely 'T(L̄)' or 'T_∞(L̄)' (Tate module of roots of unity), matching T_∞(K̄).
(28) should read I_{x'} ⊂ Π^{L̄}_{L/K} (capital Π as on the previous page) rather than π.
Marginal note 2 is better read: 'si car. k(x) est nulle — sinon groupe de ses ℓ-adiques...', referring to the tame/ℓ-adic part of inertia in positive characteristic.
Page number written at the bottom left is 117; the archive pagination of these notes runs alongside the author's own numbering (58 and 57 on the neighbouring pages).
